clue.text: Fantastic advance press surrounding one computer game

indicators.note: something fantastic is fanciful and unreal, so the letters it qualifies are freely rearranged
surrounding means the reworked letters wrap around the following piece

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A newspaper story raves about an exciting early press preview of a new computer game.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters spell SPACE NVADERS, and the I slips in to complete SPACE INVADERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Space Invaders is the classic 1978 arcade shooting game, so it is an example of a computer game.

clue.text: Careless secret agent seen around dock

indicators.note: around tells us the first word's letters are placed on both sides of the next piece

blocks.note: a spy is a secret agent
to dock a tail is to lop it, cut it short

explanation.surface: A clumsy spy is spotted loitering near the harbour dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dock' suggests a harbour, but it is the verb meaning cut short. S(LOP)PY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloppy work is slapdash and lacking care, a straightforward synonym for careless.

clue.text: Arab's tale about ornamental material

indicators.note: about here means turned around or mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Arabian storyteller spins a yarn about a decorative stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a soft translucent stone carved into vases and statues, so it is a decorative substance.

clue.text: Composer Edward dismissing a "green" artist

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so a letter is removed from the composer's name

blocks.note: Sir Edward Elgar, the English composer
the letter to be dropped
eco- is the prefix for green, environmentally friendly things

explanation.surface: A composer gets rid of an inexperienced artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the A from ELGAR to leave ELGR, then add ECO.
explanation.definitionFit: El Greco was the Cretan-born painter of the Spanish Renaissance, so he is an example of an artist.

clue.text: Hold small section of newspaper for lofty tribute

blocks.note: a nelson is a wrestling hold
S is the abbreviation for small
a column is a regular section of a newspaper

explanation.surface: An editor keeps back a little space in the paper for a grand tribute piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold' looks like a verb, but it is the wrestling grip. Nelson's Column is a monument in Trafalgar Square, London.
explanation.definitionFit: The monument honours Admiral Nelson and stands over 50 metres tall, so it is literally a towering tribute.

clue.text: Greeting nearly everyone leads to others having anxiety

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is cut
leads are the front runners, so only the opening letter of each following word is taken

blocks.note: everyone is ALL, here missing its last letter
the initial letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Greeting almost everyone makes some people nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloha is the Hawaiian word used to say hello or goodbye, so it is a greeting.

clue.text: Finally, whistle for extra time

indicators.note: finally points at the end, so the closing letter of each word is taken

blocks.note: the final letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A referee at last blows the whistle to signal extra time.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a football match; 'extra time' splits so that only 'time' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a period of history, so it is a span of time.

clue.text: American uncle restraining police inspector's cruelty

indicators.note: restraining means holding in, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: Uncle Sam personifies the United States
DI is a Detective Inspector, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: An American relative holds back a police officer who is behaving cruelly.
explanation.walkthrough: SA(DIS)M: a DI is a Detective Inspector in British police ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadism is taking pleasure in inflicting pain, which is cruelty.

clue.text: Ape's unfinished fruit

indicators.note: unfinished means lacking its end, so the last letter of the word goes

blocks.note: an orange is a fruit, here cut short

explanation.surface: A monkey leaves its fruit half-eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Orang is a short form of orang-utan, the great ape of Borneo and Sumatra.

clue.text: Old sailor wearing light stretchy garment

indicators.note: a body wearing clothes is inside them, so the first pieces sit within the next

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
tar is an old word for a sailor
an LED is a light-emitting diode

explanation.surface: An elderly seaman squeezes into a figure-hugging outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' is a noun here, the modern lamp component, not the adjective for weight; 'tar' is the classic crossword sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A leotard is a close-fitting elastic one-piece worn by dancers and gymnasts.

clue.text: Put band on initially that isn't the Cure

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letters of the two words count

blocks.note: to put something is to place it
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone asks a DJ to play a track by a band other than The Cure.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cure is a British rock band, and 'band' nudges toward music; in fact the definition is about medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy treatment with no active drug, so it is something that is not really a remedy.

clue.text: Remains overseas, hesitating to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means partly, so the solution is a part of the words nearby

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone stays abroad, uncertain about coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' reads as a verb, stays; it is the noun for what is left after cremation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashes are the remains left after a body is cremated.

clue.text: They regularly cultivated a garden shrub

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is kept
cultivated soil is dug and turned over, so the following letters are reworked

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Some people have planted a bush in their garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The hydrangea is a flowering bush with large round heads of blooms, an example of a shrub.

clue.text: Stolen Tesla reused or trashed

indicators.note: something trashed is wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: T is the symbol for the tesla, the SI unit of magnetic flux density
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stolen electric car was reused or vandalised.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesla looks like the car maker; it is the unit, giving its symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouser money is informal British for pocketing it, often dishonestly, so trousered can mean taken or stolen.

clue.text: Plant in borders of rosebush, you dig?

indicators.note: borders are the edges, so only the outermost letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters
U is text-speak for you
a dig is a barb, a cutting remark

explanation.surface: A gardener asks whether you would dig a plant into the edge of a rose bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig' plays on gardening, but it is the noun for a sly insult.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb is a garden plant grown for its edible pink stalks.

clue.text: In the current circumstances key protest mostly succeeded

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: A is a musical key
a sit-in is a protest, here missing its last letter
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: Under present conditions an important demonstration largely worked.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'as it is' means given the way things stand at present.

clue.text: Earth under separate grave

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means placed below, so this piece comes after the next one

blocks.note: to sever is to cut apart, separate
E is the abbreviation for earth

explanation.surface: Soil is piled beneath a lone burial plot.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'under' puts the earth below the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave as an adjective means serious, and severe is a synonym.

clue.text: Small branch emptied shop equipment

indicators.note: emptied means the inside is cleared out, leaving only the outer letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters
a rig is a set of equipment

explanation.surface: A twig is all that is left after the shop's fittings were cleared out.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small stem or twig with leaves, cut from a plant.

clue.text: Chap outside hotel somewhere in Belgium

indicators.note: outside means one piece sits around the other

blocks.note: a gent is a gentleman, a chap
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man waits outside his hotel on a trip to Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghent is a historic city in Flanders, so it is a place in Belgium.

clue.text: Change value to produce eggs

indicators.note: change means alter, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to adjust a setting so that more eggs are laid.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end with no link word; every other letter comes from the two words after the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To ovulate is to release an egg cell from the ovary.

clue.text: Greek character taking in clever artistic scene

indicators.note: taking in means absorbing, so one piece is put inside the other

blocks.note: tau is a letter of the Greek alphabet
able means capable, clever

explanation.surface: A Greek person with a bright mind poses for a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a picturesque grouping of figures, as in a painting or a staged scene.

clue.text: I don't like that bad smell, love

blocks.note: BO is body odour
love is nil, the letter O, in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: Someone recoils from an unpleasant odour, addressing their partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Boo is the noise an audience makes to show disapproval, matching the exclamation of dislike.

clue.text: Contend with king gripped by fever

indicators.note: gripped by means held inside, so this piece goes within the next

blocks.note: ague is an old word for a malarial fever
R is for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch battles a feverish illness.
explanation.walkthrough: A(R)GUE: the king sits inside the fever.
explanation.definitionFit: To contend can mean to assert or maintain in debate, which is to argue.

clue.text: Making film with British playboy's vintage car

blocks.note: shooting is filming a movie
B is the abbreviation for British
a rake is a dissolute pleasure-seeker, a playboy

explanation.surface: A movie shoot features a British playboy and his classic automobile.
explanation.walkthrough: A shooting brake is a British term for an estate car (station wagon) with a long rear section; older examples are now collectors' pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a vehicle for carrying hunting parties, the shooting brake survives today mainly as a classic car.
